annotations.annotation_text: Polysyllabic thunderclap on page 314 ("The Tavern"): one of ten 100-letter words synthesizing thunder across world languages, signaling a Viconian cataclysm within HCE behind the bar at his Chapelizod pub, the Norwegian Captain tale, the television broadcast, the twelve customers drinking and judging. This divine acoustic blast — fusing Hindi, Greek, Latin, French, Italian, Irish, and Norse roots — marks a civilizational transition in the Age of Heroes phase.
sources: Vico, Giambattista. Scienza Nuova (On the Thunder). https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/vico/
Atherton, James S. The Books at the Wake. https://archive.org/details/booksatwake0000athe

annotations.annotation_text: Fall/resurrection motif "ladder" on page 314 ("The Tavern"): Tim Finnegan tumbling from his ladder, Humpty Dumpty shattering from the wall, Adam falling in Eden — all converge within HCE behind the bar at his Chapelizod pub, the Norwegian Captain tale, the television broadcast, the twelve customers drinking and judging. The comic-cosmic Fall during the Age of Heroes phase demands its counterpart: resurrection through the whiskey-splash of the water of life (uisce beatha).
sources: The Ballad of Tim Finnegan's Wake. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finnegan%27s_Wake
Atherton, James S. The Books at the Wake. https://archive.org/details/booksatwake0000athe
Opie, Iona and Peter. The Oxford Dictionary of Nursery Rhymes. https://archive.org/details/oxforddictionary0000unse_m4u1
